B: Hi there, can you hear me alright?
A: Oh, yes, hiya. Sorry, I was just checking the sound. I'm Joanne.
B: Gareth. Nice to meet you, Joanne. Where are you based?
A: Sutton-in-Ashfield, in Notts. It's, erm, near Mansfield, if that helps.
B: Yeah, I know roughly where that is. I'm in Chelmsford, so Essex. What do you do?
A: I'm a kitchen assistant at a primary school. Prepping veg, serving dinners, washing up, that sort of thing. It's not very exciting, sorry.
B: No, don't apologise. Feeding a few hundred kids by twelve o'clock sounds pretty high pressure to me, to be honest.
A: It is, a bit, when it's busy. You get to know them all, which ones have allergies and that. And they won't eat anything green, so you're sort of fighting a losing battle with the broccoli.
B: Ha, yeah. I was the same as a kid, to be fair.
A: What about you?
B: I'm a travel consultant. Independent agency, tailor-made trips, mostly Japan, South-East Asia and Southern Africa. So I'm putting together itineraries, flights, transfers, hotels, all down to the hour. And I get to go and see a lot of the places, which is the nice part. I've been to Japan five times now. Kyoto in November, with the autumn leaves, honestly, it's something else.
A: Oh, that must be lovely. Is that your photo behind you, the street one?
B: It is, yeah. I took that in Gion, early morning before the tourists got up.
A: It's really good. I like how it's black and white, it sort of makes it look older, you know.
B: Thanks. That was the idea. You've got an eye for it.
A: Oh, I don't know about that. I do a bit of painting, that's all. Just at the kitchen table.
B: Is that one of yours, the robin?
A: Erm, yeah. It is, actually. I didn't think you'd see it.
B: It's really good. What do you paint mostly?
A: Birds, mostly, and trees, and old buildings round here. Watercolours. I'm not trained or anything, I just sort of muddle along. I don't know if that makes sense.
B: It makes total sense. Do you travel much yourself?
A: Not really. Caravan at Skegness, usually. I've been to Spain and Majorca. I'd love to see Rome one day, or Iceland.
B: Iceland's brilliant, yeah? The light up there would be amazing for painting. I've got a couple of clients going in the autumn, actually. You'd want to do it in September, avoid the summer prices.
A: I'll have to save up a fair bit first, I think.
B: Fair enough. It can be done on a budget, though, if you're sensible about it.
A: Maybe. Gary would want to know where the chippy is.
B: Is Gary your husband?
A: Partner, yeah. Eleven years. He's a forklift driver, he's not really one for abroad.
B: Right. Well, there are worse things than Skegness and a nice...
